name: Lavenders (LAVNDR120)
overview: Lavenders reveals consumer behaviour: what people actually order, when, and from which businesses, drawn from the real orders of 120 businesses and brands, turned into a live index (LAVNDR120) and reports for businesses and brands. Lavenders is a digital market system that brings together 120 businesses and brands in one market; each business runs its own order-management app (OMS), and their real orders feed one live consumer index called LAVNDR120. Lavenders is the brand; LAVNDR120 is the index. Unrelated to lavender plants or oil.
disclaimers: No buying, selling or trading of shares on the platform.
Informational only: not investment advice and no promise of profit or returns.
Terms and agreements are drafts pending legal review.
Prices are as of 1 November 2026; the home page is the source of truth.

faq.a: Lavenders reveals consumer behaviour: what people actually order, when, and from which businesses, drawn from the real orders of 120 businesses and brands, turned into a live index (LAVNDR120) and reports for businesses and brands. It is a digital market system that brings together 120 businesses and brands in one market. Each business runs its own order-management app (OMS).

faq.q: What consumer behaviour does Lavenders reveal?
faq.a: Lavenders reads the real orders of the 120 businesses and brands in a market: which products and services are requested most, how order activity moves over time, and how the market behaves as a whole. This is shown as a live consumer index (LAVNDR120), read-only market data (Lava) and a forecasting report on market behaviour (Vindex). It is descriptive information only, with no promise of profit or returns.

faq.q: What is the difference between Lavenders and LAVNDR120?
faq.a: Lavenders is the name of the system and the brand. LAVNDR120 is the name of its consumer index.
It is the number of businesses and brands in each market.
No. There is no buying, selling or trading of shares inside the platform. The index measures the real order activity of the businesses.

faq.q: Is this investment advice or a promise of returns?
faq.a: No. The information is descriptive only. There is no promise of profit or returns, and any participation is subject to the platform's terms and agreements.

faq.q: Is Lavenders related to lavender plants?
faq.a: No. The name is a brand for a digital market system and has nothing to do with lavender plants or oil.

faq.q: What do visitors who have not subscribed see?
faq.a: Only the real index card. Other screens show demo data for visitors and real data for subscribers.

faq.q: How does a business or brand join?
faq.a: See the OMS package and the Economic Movement path on the packages page.

faq.q: What is the Lavenders app builder?
faq.a: A tool inside Lavenders that builds an order store for a business: a web store and an Android app, created automatically inside the business owner's own Google account (Apps Script backend, Google Sheet for orders, images in Drive). Each store runs for 24 hours as a trial; the publishable version unlocks with an active OMS, Reseller or Franchise membership.

faq.q: What is the golden certificate in Lavenders?
faq.a: An optional certificate that a business in Lavenders may request from the index operating fund. Its founding value is based on the business's own documented orders. A business with at least 100 documented orders; an order counts only when documented by a tax invoice from the approved ledger. Requesting is optional. Each order is valued at $4.275. To mint the certificate the business pays 36% of the total of its approved orders in cash; this is the casting value of its golden certificate.

appBuilder.what: A tool inside Lavenders that builds an order store for a business: a web store and an Android app, created automatically inside the business owner's own Google account (Apps Script backend, Google Sheet for orders, images in Drive).
appBuilder.whoCanBuild: OMS, Reseller and Franchise members; anyone can start a 24-hour trial and publishing needs an active membership.
steps: Enter the business name and choose services or products.
Add up to 9 items; each item needs an image and a price times pack quantity of at least $4.275.
Enter bank-transfer payment details (bank, account holder, account, IBAN) and an optional local-currency rate.
Sign in with Google once; the system creates the backend, the orders sheet and the image folder in the owner's account.
Share the store link and build the Android app from the same screen.
appBuilder.customerFlow: A customer opens the store, taps an item, fills in the order form and confirms with a one-time code sent by email that includes the bank-transfer details. The owner accepts or rejects the order from the dashboard and the customer is emailed the decision. The owner gets a notification for each new order.
appBuilder.trial: Each store runs for 24 hours as a trial; the publishable version unlocks with an active OMS, Reseller or Franchise membership.
appBuilder.dataOwnership: The store, orders and images live in the owner's own Google account. Lavenders only checks eligibility, issues the unlock code and triggers the Android build.
appBuilder.payments: Payment is a bank transfer received directly by the owner; Lavenders does not hold or process customers' money.
appBuilder.joinIndex: After unlocking, the owner can send the store's sheet with the business name to the Lavenders administration; if accepted, the business is added to the index with a link to its store.
appBuilder.android: The Android app is downloaded directly from the store page or the official site; it is not on Google Play.

goldenCertificate.what: An optional certificate that a business in Lavenders may request from the index operating fund. Its founding value is based on the business's own documented orders.
goldenCertificate.eligibility: A business with at least 100 documented orders; an order counts only when documented by a tax invoice from the approved ledger. Requesting is optional.
goldenCertificate.valuation: Each order is valued at $4.275. To mint the certificate the business pays 36% of the total of its approved orders in cash; this is the casting value of its golden certificate.
goldenCertificate.review: The Lavenders administration reviews the request; if accepted, the certificate value is shown once three verification conditions are met: financial, guarantee and documentary.
goldenCertificate.donation: A business may donate part or all of its certificate value to another business. Each side enters a phone number and a contact method; details are revealed to both only when the donation is accepted.
goldenCertificate.notIncluded: No buying, selling or trading of shares; not investment advice; no promise of profit or returns; terms and agreements are drafts pending legal review.
